Bei diesem Blogpost handelt es sich um eine Übersicht zu verschiedenen Flugzeugkomponenten

Hydraulic system

THe PTU is a hydraulic “bridge” between the green and yellow system. Its a bidirectional unit, meaning it can transfer hydraulic power in either direction, depending on which system is losing pressure

Cockpit

✅ 1. Static Ports (center-right, inside the red outline)

These small holes labeled F/O (First Officer) and CAPT (Captain) are static ports. They measure static air pressure, which is used for:

Altitude (altimeter)

Vertical speed (VSI)

Airspeed indicator (together with pitot tubes)

The red box around them says:

“STATIC PORTS – DO NOT PLUG OR DEFORM HOLES. Area within red line must be smooth and clean.”

This is crucial, because blocking static ports has caused fatal aircraft accidents (e.g., Birgenair 301).

✅ 2. Avionics Equipment Vent / Air Inlet Valve (left side)

The round panel labeled AVIONICS EQPT VENT AIR INLET VALVE is part of the cooling system for the aircraft’s avionics (electronics). It pulls in air to cool the computers below the cockpit. The “CAUTION – HIGH AIR FLOW INTAKE” warning means that strong suction may occur while systems are running.

Fly by Wire system (electrical)

Cables and Pulleys move stearing components. Since 1930s there are fly-by-wire planes. Russian manufacturer Tupolev developed the first FBW System Movement of joystick => gets converted into digital signal (ELAC1 Elvevator and Aileron Computer) (ELAC2) Airbus “Normal Law” doesnt allow extreme and unsave plane movements Same stick input also lead to the same aircraft rotations because airplane speed is considered in the calculation of the ELAC system. Overwing Emergency doors

It is easier to fly an airbus than a boeing.

mechanical cables are heavy. A fly by wire-system reduces weight.
